This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation has a direct linear relationship with the Cauchy matrix scheme variables S0,0 and S1,0. A detailed analysis of the Lax pair and Bäcklund transformation has been carried out. Additionally, two new forms of the Bäcklund transformation have been derived, which allow for the generation of multiple solutions of the equation. The study also explores the soliton solution of the equation and finds it relates to the soliton of the KP equation.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect relationships being easily identified due to poor object detection. As a result, the network fails to grasp the complexity of more subtle inaccuracies. Our analysis also reveals that overfitting is significant in VRD as seen in the current approaches. To overcome these challenges, we introduce our novel method Multi-Task Multi-Stage Network with Regularization (M2S3R). It employs a multi-task network structure and a novel regularization technique called relationship-foreground matching (RfM) to align the vRelDet network with the detection network and enhance its sensitivity to difficult relationship proposals. Our experiments demonstrate that M2S3R yields substantial improvements, reducing the false positive rate by 41.4% and achieving a new state-of-the-art performance on the COCO dataset. The code for this model can be found at https://github.com/Cheng-Wei-Chang/M2S3R.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost (QCC), quantifies the amount of quantum correlation employed in weak measurement procedures utilizing the trace norm. It's demonstrated that the QCC is directly linked to the trace-norm-based quantum discord (TQD) by a factor dependent on weak measurement strength. However, since TQD is not confined by quantum correlations in all instances, the QCC is found to exceed certain bounds in situations where no quantum correlation is present, specifically occurring when a system is traced out by a complementary subsystem. Notably, the QCC is shown to be capable of detecting post-entanglement quantum correlations that TQD is not able to recognize.

Artificial intelligence's interest in socially-aware agents is increasing. To address this, agents require an understanding of social relationships and behaviors, which can be summarized in a graph. Developing a automatic understanding of entities' social connections through learning from examples is challenging due to a lack of annotated datasets. While current methods are limited to analyzing existing relationship graphs, an emerging need exists for systems that can automatically create social relationship graphs from raw data, particularly text descriptions of social networks. This problem is tackled in this research, where an end-to-end social relationship graph generation approach is proposed and demonstrated effective in initial experiments.

Capturing long-range relationships in scene understanding tasks is a crucial goal in computer vision. While self-attention mechanisms effectively model global relationships, they come with high computational costs and hinder real-time applications. Gating mechanisms also provide dynamic relationships but are limited in processing only immediate temporal or spatial contexts. In contrast, graph neural networks can efficiently pass local information and extend it to global levels through multi-layered connections. However, existing graph neural networks struggle to dynamicize the relationship passing process. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts the relationship passing process in graph neural networks by integrating a gating mechanism. This results in better performance compared to existing scene understanding models that use attention or recursive message passing for dynamic relationships. Moreover, our model offers significant computational efficiency benefits when used in image regions, enabling practical real-time applications.

Optimizing hardware cost is critical in digital circuit design, where efficient multiplication of multiple constants is a complex task.  Currently, there's no established method to handle this optimization effectively.  To address this issue, we've developed an algorithm designed to optimize the hardware cost of constant multiplications.  This approach utilizes a linear program to find the optimal shift and add tree structure, employing an automatically generated database that connects each input constant to its output. We've successfully tested the program on a comprehensive set of DSP input constants drawn from real-world applications and major benchmark suites, and the results have shown our approach to outperform existing methods in both additionals and multipliers hardware costs. Furthermore, the results have also indicated the feasibility of integrating this methodology into existing Electronic Design Automation tools.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural networks, paving the way for widespread adoption. This paper delves into the foundational aspects and core principles of quantum deep learning, highlighting key breakthroughs along the way. It also explores the challenges inherent in quantum deep learning research from multiple viewpoints, followed by a discussion of prospective future directions and practical applications.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology continues to be the core of both existing and newly proposed facilities, spanning research areas from direct-Cernn most compact colliders to compact collider proposals, beam dynamics and accelerators beyond protons, as well as intensity frontier, low intensity, and neutrino experiments.  The radio frequency accelerator technology remains the critical driving force behind improvements in energy efficiency for green experiments and the precise control of beam emittance for experiments focusing on the front of both low and high intensities.  This is particularly apparent in the development of new beam concepts, including radio frequency superconducting, electron cooling and normal conducting accelerators.  The ongoing research and development in radio frequency accelerator technology will continue to significantly contribute to the advancement of the accelerator community and the broader physics research community.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles of a future muon collider, along with the technical and physical obstacles that need to be addressed for its realization. The discussion then moves on to examine the current advancements and research linked to a muon collider project, highlighting key milestones and milestones that could translate theoretical concepts into tangible outcomes.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. Our comparison also shows that these two methods produce analogous results to the first and second order causal Navier-Stokes theories. Notably, the relaxation-time-approximation model yields stable tensor modes in all cases, whereas divergence-based models result in tensor mode instability for certain classes of theories. Furthermore, in both approximate orders, our hydrodynamic relations align with the kinetic theory's quasi-classical sound wave dispersion.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes could be the source behind the observed excess radiowave signals. By assuming that dark matter exists entirely as these black holes, we calculated that the resulting Hawking radiation could match the observed signals in the GMRT LSRP experiment. However, this hypothesis faces challenges due to constraints imposed by recent direct-detection experiments, which show that the interaction cross-section of dark matter particles must be significantly lower than what would be required for the primordial black holes to account for the excess radiowave signals.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together multi-opcode general-purpose sequential processing with Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to enable Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) at a secure computing offloading level, such as cloud computing. The VSP safeguardingly shields both input data and function evaluations against adversaries in a secure computing offloading scenario like cloud computing. To enhance performance, our innovative VSP architecture features five stages: a carrier extraction module, an intricate function network module comprising a complex network and an adder network, a control module, an accumulated vector module, and a result extraction module. Notably, the high parallelism of our design significantly contributes to its exceptional efficiency. Through a comprehensive analysis, the results of our experiments verify the feasibility of the VSP's design, highlighting its superiority over existing approaches like Secret Sharing (SS)-based approaches in terms of execution time per input and communication time. Specifically, the execution time per input exhibits a linear growth with the number of secret parties under constant numbers of circuit depth and TFHE plaintext modulus bits. Building upon a comprehensive processor design consisting of a 5-stage pipeline, registers, an instruction fetch unit, an instruction decode unit, an execution unit, a write-back unit, and an instruction fetch module, the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our design through benchmarks such as single loop multiplication and loop multiplication with accumulation and comparison with a non-secure counterpart. Moreover, the performance of our design

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover when restricted to certain parameters, which are examples of unary constraints. While some studies have established results for binary constraints with particular structures, the general-valued case with low-degree constraints remains an open question. The research presents a general framework for PTAS constructs applicable to multi-dimensional counting problems, built upon Sharifzadeh and Wrochna's work and incorporating Karp-Sipser graph degree reduction. The framework is successfully applied to the sparse general-valued CSP instance, yielding a PTAS and answering a question raised by Buchbinder et al. Furthermore, it shows that an FPTAS can be achieved for certain tasks with dimensionality one and totally monotone constraints. The framework has also been made publicly available on the GitHub platform.

Pre-trained language models possess the ability to capture syntactical information to a significant extent, as suggested by previous studies. This has led to the development of a new approach where the creation of syntax trees can be directly optimized from pre-trained models like BERT and BART. We explore the effectiveness of this approach in the context of parsing tasks, including the potential of using pre-trained models to accurately predict the syntax of unseen languages with minimal annotated data. Our method rivals the state-of-the-art performance on well-established parsing datasets and achieves remarkable cross-lingual generalization, outperforming alternative methods when applied to languages from different language families. This research provides strong evidence that pre-trained language models can effectively capture syntactical information across a wide range of languages.

High-definition hyperspectral images possess the unique capability to distinguish between diverse objects within intricate environments by analyzing each pixel across various frequency ranges. Although HSI cameras are becoming increasingly accessible, extracting accurate object information from these images presents a significant challenge. In contrast, numerous deep learning methods have been developed for cityscape object segmentation, leveraging annotated images with pixel-level detail to segment objects effectively. However, such annotations are expensive to obtain, while unsupervised methods lack the necessary training guidance to yield satisfactory results. In this research, an innovative approach is proposed that utilizes hyperspectral data from an unsupervised source and limited supervised information from image levels to perform cityscape object segmentation. By combining this pre-trained model with hand-crafted features and leveraging the structural cues from superspectral images, a novel pixel-level representation is introduced that significantly outperforms conventional approaches despite lacking supervised training. Furthermore, this research explores the potential of incorporating superspectral data into existing segmentation models even when superspectral data is unavailable, thereby minimizing the dependence on supervised annotations by leveling up the unstructured and supervised information.

This study reveals striking evidence of interaction between a planet and its host star, showcasing a rare state where the star is oblate and spinning at high speed despite its age. We discovered such a state for HD86101, characterized by abnormal rotation and distinct chemical composition and surface abundance patterns, all likely the result of a planet ingestion. In particular, the surface abundances of a wide range of elements hint at the engagement of CNO and other stellar processes, implying that the ingested planet had at least a moderately massive atmosphere. Another significant finding is the unusually high levels of Ph and Fe on the star, which can only be explained by direct planet ingestion. However, the presence of angular momentum contradictions suggests that the final planetary disruption might have occurred far in the past, and the current star planet abundance pattern may have been achieved through internal stellar processes.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and referred to as the RAM model, where there are no explicitly stated assumptions. However, one fundamental question that remains unanswered is the set of basic arithmetic operations that can be executed in constant time within this computation model, given that addition is already assumed to be instant.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new approach exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the success of this innovative method in achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmark datasets.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to a subring of $n \times n$ matrices, resulting in LCD codes that are also group codes due to being ideals in a group ring. Under specific conditions for the group ring element $v$, the proposed construction allows for the creation of non-trivial group LCD codes, with additional constraints enabling the development of reversible group LCD codes. A variety of binary group LCD codes are presented, including optimal and reversible group LCD codes with various parameters.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the metric graph moduli space, derived by mapping invariant differential forms from the tropical Abel-Jacobi line bundle. Although our compactification diverges from the Casson-Lefschetz-Payne-Peters line bundle, it offers a concrete connection to graphs and facilitates the computation of its cohomology via the Petersson decomposition. Notably, these differential forms can be employed to create generalised Feynman integrals, extending the method initially proposed for graph complexes by Fock and Goncharov.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of RNN recurrence in aiding object categorization.  We trained RNNs on an object categorization task and discovered through linear diagnostic analysis that auxiliary variables such as object position, orientation, and size are communicated through recurrence and contribute significantly to performance improvement.  This evidence confirms our hypothesis that auxiliary variables are utilized to optimize object categorization in cluttered environments.

Despite numerous studies on non-Hermitian topology, the influence of correlations remains a significant unresolved issue. We conducted an in-depth analysis of correlated systems in one-dimensional non-Hermitian Haldane models with interactions. Our results reveal that correlations significantly alter the topological characteristics, causing a shift from one and zero trivial phases as the interaction strength varies, all within a framework fully supported by analytical findings. Unlike previous studies focused on integrable systems, our analysis is not restricted to specific cases, providing valuable insights into the role of correlations in more complex systems of interest.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional arrays by introducing three novel constructions for multi-phase GCAs of dimension $F^d$, specifically for $d=2$ where $F$ is any prime power, and $d=3$ with $F$ being a square prime power, and $d=3$ for prime $F$.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining CMS data from 13 TeV LHC and previously collected data from 7 and 13 TeV, totaling 100 fb^-1. The dataset in the four-lepton final state enables the measurement of Higgs boson production rates both on and near its resonance peak, facilitating the determination of its coupling strength to gauge and Higgs fields. The observed production pattern aligns with predictions, showing significant deviations in the on-shell region. The Higgs boson width is estimated, combined with factors influencing its interaction with these bosons, based both on the observed data and through Bayesian analysis of the differential distributions.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, we investigate several deep convolutional autoencoders with feature fusion that perform unsupervised change detection on multispectral and hyperspectral remote sensing images. These encoders, consisting of multiple layers, are trained using their own unsupervised objectives. During training, we integrate a feature fusion module that merges the extracted multi-scale features from each encoder layer, and evaluate both the conventional and proposed methods using their respective reconstruction errors. Our results demonstrate that the proposed unsupervised change detection technique outperforms existing methodologies, and the fusion of multi-scale features enhances the accuracy of the results.

Consider the set $\mathcal{S}$ which contains all square numbers and all positive integer pairs $(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A})$ such that no two elements from $\mathcal{S}$ add up to any element in $\mathcal{A}$. We demonstrate that, for large $\mathcal{S}$ up to a certain value, the maximum sum of elements in $\mathcal{A}$ is bounded above by $O(N^{1/2} (\log N)^2)$. This finding supports a conjecture by Tomaszewski.

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that can be triggered by lattice disturbances within insulating barriers. By applying a gate, we can control the L-valley interference in silicon atoms as the electronic wavefunctions merge and the tunneling probability increases and decreases accordingly. This effect can be observed at a level comparable to the lattice structure by employing lattice-sensitive L-valley interference measurements. Furthermore, we have demonstrated the capability to map the L-valley phase coherence length across regions affected by tunneling at atomic dimensions by adjusting the level of coupling between adjacent silicon samples. This additional capability allows us to examine the influence of localized plasmons on coherence properties and to infer the conditions under which electron-hole interactions decay within silicon junctions at a temperature of 4 Kelvin.

A wide array of optimization techniques, such as quadratic programming and
stochastic optimization methods like projected gradient descent, plays a vital
role in numerous real-life applications including online advertising and robotics.
However, the growing demand for these methods in control systems and dynamical
systems necessitates their development into increasingly sophisticated and
sophisticated designs. As a result, the practical implementation of these
optimization algorithms becomes challenging due to the need for efficient and
reliable software frameworks. In the absence of a unified, intuitive open-source
software framework, the implementation and comparison of optimization algorithms
becomes a daunting task. In the effort to address this issue, we introduce
LibOPT, an intuitive and modular open-source Python framework facilitating the
rapid prototyping and implementation of various optimization algorithms. By
leveraging a headless architecture and efficient data structures, the LibOPT
framework enables the easy integration and development of new optimization
algorithms while providing the functionality for seamless serialization and
deserialization of algorithm objects for future reuse. Furthermore, the library
is supported by a comprehensive set of built-in, state-of-the-art optimization
algorithms and tools for model prediction correction and nonlinear control. In
the libOPT framework, all developed and integrated algorithms are systematically
evaluated against several benchmark problems to ensure their effectiveness and
efficiency, which in turn enables the easy reproduction and verification of
results using the provided scripts. In the framework's comprehensive
implementation, the libOPT

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are described by non-abelian space symmetries represented by a four-momentum group. Our approach recognizes that the definitions used for scattering and transport processes in previous studies are incompatible. Nevertheless, we propose a systematic theory of identity loss based on an alternative, self-consistent definition of momentum. Using vector matrices for particle states, we reinterpret the on-shell condition, which becomes a matrix equation. Consequently, our formalism has implications for the understanding of non-commutative space-time effects on scattering processes. As a case study, we examine the impact of identity loss on a two-particle scattering process and calculate the S-matrix. Our analysis reveals that the order of matrix multiplication in the S-matrix corresponds to the order in which particles interact.

We apply the two-photon absorption transient current technique to study
properties of wide-bandgap semiconductors with high spatial resolution. We utilize
this technique to investigate charge transport in scCVD diamond, a synthetic
diamond produced through the chemical vapor deposition process. By directing a
photon beam at an angle less than 90° relative to the sample surface, we create
a three-dimensional varying electron-hole pair generation profile. By analyzing
this profile, we calculate magnetic field-independent transient currents and map the
distribution of material quality and grain orientation within the diamond sample.
Our experimental results reveal the structure of thick diamond layers and
demonstrate the ability to study vertical charge transport. The technique also
yields a measured value for saturation drift velocity of 10^7 cm/s in the diamond
sample. Additionally, it allows us to detect microcracks and grain boundaries and
investigate their influence on charge transport. By comparing our findings with
those of conventional electrical measurements and simulations, we demonstrate the
advantage of the two-photon absorption transient current technique in obtaining
comprehensive information on charge transport in diamond material, which can be
applied to other wide-bandgap semiconductors as well.

This study tackles the under-resourced challenges of identifying and categorizing
harmful online behaviors toward women in the Persian Gulf region. By building on
existing English models, we adapt them to detect and classify written texts that
express online misogyny among Arabic speakers. Our research introduces a comprehensive
taxonomy of the region's unique cultural forms of online misogyny, encompassing
stereotypes about women's capabilities, alleged moral failures, and their
enforced subordinate status. We develop a robust dataset comprising manually
curated examples from online social media platforms and employ an ensemble of
advanced natural language processing models. Our findings offer valuable insights
into the efficacy of these models and their application in addressing local
issues. Our data, annotations, and taxonomy are openly accessible for further
study: https://osf.io/7vp6y

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We introduce a novel model-based reinforcement learning method, called Probabilistic Distributional Policy Search (PDPS), that leverages a neural network to predict the state transition probability distribution and employs it to optimize control policies, aiming to maximize long-term cumulative rewards in stochastic environments. The probability distribution is approximated and stored as a probability mass function using neural networks, which offers a significant advantage: it allows for the direct computation of robust control policies, less susceptible to environment perturbations, without the need to generate additional samples. The method performs well experimentally and exhibits a notable benefit: even when the simulated environment model is corrupted with noise, robust controllers are still possible.

Several key network communication challenges such as caching and computation are interconnected. A centralized caching model was initially developed by Kadhe et al., allowing a single server to serve multiple users. This model was later extended to include multiple servers. Concurrently, a distributed computation model was studied by Khrebti and Shah, initially with one server. These frameworks provided valuable insights but were limited to specific network conditions. To address a broader range network scenarios, we have created a unified framework that combines both caching and computation. Our unified framework allows for the analysis of various network conditions and has shown that schemes developed under the unified framework generalize and provide new perspectives on existing schemes. This unified framework provides a range of parameters for network configuration and has provided the capacity to analyze and compare different caching and computation strategies. To illustrate, we have shown that our unified framework can accommodate a extended version of the popular Zero-Zeros scheme from Kadhe et al. In addition, we have developed a new unified computation scheme and found it offers performance benefits over existing schemes such as Khrebtii's. Our unified framework provides a new and flexible approach to network conditions and has provided a deeper understanding of the relationships between caching and computation.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in univalent type theory, adopting a constructive and predicative framework. To capture the essence of non-terminating processes in PCF, we employ the lifting monad from topos theory, which has been adapted for univalent type theory by Escard\'o and Knapp. Our work confirms that using the lifting monad provides a viable way to handle partiality within univalent type theory, and we also demonstrate that a predicative and constructive Scott model is achievable. Notably, we avoid reliance on choice or quotient inductive-inductive types, unlike other approaches. We hold that our model aligns with the current capabilities of univalent type theory and offers valuable insights into dealing with partiality.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots remains a key challenge, particularly when accounting for the robot's spatial structure.
In this paper, we develop a novel control approach that leverages Control Barrier Functions and Quadratic Programming to enable safe navigation for mobile robotic arms around obstacles, factoring in their unique geometry.
Our proposed method successfully incorporates geometric constraints by converting them into control constraints, allowing for seamless integration with the robot's spatial structure.
Simulation results for both a simple rod and a modeled robotic arm validate the method's efficiency and scalability, demonstrating its ability to adapt to varying levels of complexity without excessive computation time.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have shown great interest in the capabilities of Bose-Einstein condensates, particularly due to their potential for executing complex quantum algorithms and representing quantum information through spatial or temporal conditions. However, most research has been limited to analyzing the effects of linear Bose-Hubbard models, leaving a need to develop and study nonlinear quantum gates. This work aims to fill this gap by introducing a method to create nonlinear quantum gates using the conditions of a Bose-Einstein condensate, specifically utilizing the non-constant interaction between atoms in a Bose-Hubbard model. The study presents a quantum circuit to demonstrate a nonlinear controlled-NOT gate, showing that it can function efficiently under two distinct scenarios - when using coupling constants related to inter-atomic interactions or optical effects. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the proposed nonlinear gate performs better than its linear counterpart in controlling errors, particularly when relating to coupling constants and phonon phenomena.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications due to its ability to convert nonlinear systems into a set of equations that can be solved without losing essential information. A solution to such a system is considered geometrically meaningful if it is nondegenerate, meaning the Jacobian matrix at the solution has full rank. Our work builds upon the signature-based algorithm to efficiently compute nondegenerate locus and solutions of a given polynomial system. Our enhancements to the algorithm involve several aspects, including the optimization of Macaulay matrix computation, identification and utilization of invariant conditions to simplify computation, and a Groebner basis-based method to verify nondegeneracy of obtained solutions. Through extensive testing with the SINGULAR software, our improved algorithm demonstrates considerable speed improvements, achieving speedups of up to 1,000 times, and enables the calculation of nondegenerate locus for polynomial systems with up to 17 variables and 30 equations. Moreover, our approach can be applied to solve systems arising from locating geometric configurations, such as those used in geometric solvers for synthetic geometry.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central events of Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. By creating a comprehensive model that combines direct and thermal photon signals, researchers found that the average direct photon transverse momentum is 5.16 GeV/$c$ and per unit rapidity is 17.78 per unit rapidity. Comparing experimental results to theoretical models, they discovered that the data closely matches models with an average nuclear radius that includes the effect of the skin effect in the nucleus, specifically that the average nuclear radius for $^{63}$Cu is 1.03 fm larger than the core radius. Moreover, they observed that the direct photon yield shows an exponential dependence on the inverse of the average transverse momentum as predicted by the photon emission factor model, which they found provides a consistent description of both direct and thermal photon behavior across all transverse momentum ranges.

The Turan tetrahedron problem seeks to determine the maximum number of edges in a graph lacking a complete subgraph of four vertices. In 1966, Chvatal and Rolfsen suggested constructing a maximal such graph by using a three-dimensional grid and proposed that the number of edges could be calculated using a formula based on the graph's vertices. However, the validity of this formula remained unproven until now. In an alternative formulation of the problem, we prove that this maximal graph's number of edges is indeed given by that three-dimensional formula, specifically by showing that the graph's edges are calculated using a formula based on the graph's vertices. This was achieved by utilizing an inequality that generalizes a well-known result about the sum of square roots.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing algorithm that combines high quality and low computational cost. However, current solutions designed for high-frame-rate animations do not effectively address the challenge of rendering large vector maps, necessitating a novel anti-aliasing algorithm tailored to this specific use case. This algorithm only anti-aliases the edge pixels of lines within the visible viewport, leveraging a priority-based approach that utilizes a customized binary heap to identify high-priority pixels first. By employing an average-based color calculation method, the algorithm generates target colors for edge pixels and refines pixel values using a efficient subtraction method that utilizes an accumulation array. Our proposed anti-aliasing algorithm produces performance improvements totaling 300% and yields effects comparable to a high-quality algorithm while delivering exceptional effects at lower costs.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on the Wu-Schaback quasi-interpolation formula, we adapt this new interpolation function while preserving the original scheme's characteristics, including monotonicity and convexity. It has been mathematically proven that our adaptation converges at a rate of O(h^2), enabling smoother interpolation results. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the method's efficiency and accuracy.

Pulsar halos are large-scale, high-energy emission structures, formed when energetic electrons and positrons break free from pulsar wind nebulae. As a novel category of gamma-ray emitters, pulsar halos serve as optimal probes for examining the diffusion of cosmic rays within the Galaxy's localized areas, as well as their escape from pulsar wind nebulae. Recent breakthroughs in X-ray imaging have further enriched our comprehension of pulsar halos, enabling direct observations that had previously been limited to lower-energy electromagnetic spectrum surveys. This review focuses on recent developments concerning pulsar halos, encompassing research from theoretical and cosmic-ray physics to novel astrophysical discoveries beyond this field.

Predicting the weather is a crucial task for everyday life that extends to being a critical component for various fields. While automatic weather forecasting through deep learning has been explored in multiple studies, they primarily focused on the task of classifying four weather types. In contrast, our research presents a comprehensive approach to automatically identifying and classifying all 10 primary weather conditions using a newly created, extensively annotated dataset comprising 70,000 images of windows with weather views. This work features the compilation of an expansive window image collection, the development of a customized data enhancement technique, and in-depth evaluations of leading convolutional neural networks for window image classification. Our study shows that incorporating objects other than windows during the training process or fine-tuning pre-trained models yields substantial performance gains, contributing to a remarkable 82% consecutive improvement in weather prediction accuracy.

Our analysis examines how climate change interest shifts among diverse groups and how their individual interests interconnect. Initially, we track the individual trends, followed by developing a cross-influence model that we then validate using a VAR model. Our results indicate significant fluctuations in the general public's climate change interest, as evident from our creation of a Climate Change Index for Europe and the US based on media mentions, whereas economists show relatively little interest as measured by prominent journal publications. Interestingly, science journals and policymakers demonstrate a more sustained interest in the subject, albeit with less evidence of mutual interactions among these groups.

Soft grippers are increasingly utilized across various applications, primarily thanks to their versatility and flexibility. Nevertheless, their nonlinear properties and multi-variable nature pose significant challenges for controlling them, often making online control or modeling-and-control-separately approaches impractical due to inadequate performance. To overcome these difficulties, this research proposes a new system identification method tailored specifically for controlling soft multi-fingered grippers, leveraging the power of the Koopman operator theory. By utilizing this theoretical framework, the proposed approach effectively transforms non-linear dynamics into a manageable, high-dimensional linear one, thereby simplifying the control process. Moreover, the study introduces an online algorithm capable of estimating model parameters in real-time, thereby enabling the development of a robust model-predictive control (MPC) controller. Through various simulation and physical experiments, the proposed method is shown to surpass existing techniques and achieve excellent performance.

One of the fundamental problems in multivariate statistics involves point estimation for a general statistical model, particularly focusing on developing Torsney's multivariate distribution family. We aim to create a statistical multivariate optimization method akin to gradient descent. Our approach generalizes the concept of a Euclidean space by providing a framework that encompasses various existing non-Euclidean optimization techniques. Building on this framework, we propose an algorithm analogous to gradient descent that utilizes the Torsney information potential and integrate it with our proposed generalization. We demonstrate that this generalized method encompasses several well-known non-Euclidean optimization techniques such as Natural Gradient Descent, Riemannian Trust-Region and Manifold-Sensitive Optimization. We also provide a comprehensive theoretical analysis of the proposed technique, including proving its convergence under certain strong convexity conditions.

High-energy emissions from ancient supermassive black holes can be traced back to the early universe, especially during a critical period of intense star formation approximately one billion years after the Big Bang. A new radio source, designated J2102+6015, has been discovered at the edge of this time frame with a location far away from Earth. This object has a very high mass for its black hole and is emitting intense waves across various frequencies. Observations using the VLT and other tools reveal that it has a low mass for its black hole and is churning up dust and gas as it sits within a cloud. As these emissions shift from low-energy to high-energy, they suggest the black hole is launching jets of gas. Analysis of its far-off distances and energy patterns shows that its higher energy patterns fit a model that uses particles changing spins to create these waves. Further research will be needed to confirm the black hole's properties.

This research focuses on improving survival time prediction for lung cancer patients by exploring a combination of image analysis and patient data, such as age and tumor size. We demonstrate that integrating visual information with clinical data yields more accurate results. Furthermore, we've conducted a comprehensive analysis of different model architectures and features on a public dataset of lung cancer patients. The prediction performance of our proposed model is evaluated at the 2019 Brain Imaging and Pathology Machine Learning Challenge for Adult Cancer using a cohort of Adult Cancer patients who underwent a PET-CT scan and for whom clinical information is available.

A well-designed state representation is crucial in the learning process of Reinforcement Learning. Natural language can be utilized in numerous tasks to either represent the state or constitute it entirely. This overview focuses on the techniques employed by researchers to create natural language state representations, underscoring the need for more transparent and contextualized models, thorough justification of design choices and assessments of the relative effectiveness of varying methodologies.

A novel approach combining machine learning is introduced, enabling the reconstruction of cosmological density perturbations from waterfall quasars. In detail, a convolutional neural network model can yield three-dimensional matter maps spanning 290 Mpc/c in resolution with 78 wavelength lines per pixel. Preliminary results reveal that even with limited data points, our method accurately reflects large-scale structures and incorporates quantum noise. Furthermore, we have successfully fine-tuned the algorithm to produce matter maps that closely mirror those from the simulation. Ultimately, we have shown that the convolutional neural network effectively captures both the magnitude and phase information of the Fourier coefficients, thereby faithfully representing the cosmic web structure.

This paper examines certain types of non-weight modules connected to Lie algebras of the Weyl type. Firstly, we establish the characteristics of modules whose restrictions to $U(\frak h)$ are one-dimensional for the Lie algebras of differential operators. An important application of this study is the description of the points for the highest weight modules for the Lie algebras of differential operators. Additionally, we identify the points for the generalized highest weight modules. Moreover, we prove that the modules described in this paper have no submodules, are multiplicity-free, and provide a pointwise decomposition for the modules for the Lie algebras of differential operators. This study can be seen as a continuation of an earlier work by the same authors, relating to Lie algebras of vector fields.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their
competitors. As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and
challenging due to the unmodified nature of social media texts. Since social media
data is inherently sequential, RNNs and LSTMs are well-suited for this type of data.
This project utilized Keras' implementation of LSTMs to develop a Twitter sentiment
analysis model that accounts for word order, achieving a 86% accuracy rate on the Twitter
sentiment analysis dataset.

The role-defined constraint, however, has been neglected in the definition of open-domain dialogue systems. Our study aims to address this gap by examining the performance of scale-defined open-domain dialogue systems with a specific, non-standard constraint. We compare the effectiveness of various architectures, including both traditional task-based task-based tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks tasks

The binary black hole merger's aftermath leaves a lasting mark on space-time known as gravitational wave memory, and multiple events create a background of residual noise known as the stochastic gravitational wave background. This phenomenon is being explored using the background's statistical properties, and it's believed to be generated by the collective impact of binary black hole mergers. A new study shows that even when individual signals are undetectable by LIGO or similar detectors, they can still be detected as a collective whole. Moreover, it's revealed that the background generated by the early stages of these mergers dominates over the one resulting from the final stages, and in doing so, it provides insight into the binary black hole merger rate. Even with current technology, this background may offer valuable information about the universe, and future LISA and third-generation LIGO-like detectors are expected to gather a vast amount of data about this background, potentially providing precise measurements. These findings highlight the significance of analyzing the detected background independently for different frequency bands and offer new understanding of the nature of binary black hole mergers.

A hypothetical supersymmetry framework offers an explanation for baryon asymmetry through a second-order phase transition involving a large Higgs Vev, triggered by thermal corrections and resulting in nearly scale-invariant dynamics and significant departure from the standard SSB scenario with negligible Vev scales. This theoretical framework allows for the incorporation of supergravity and left-right symmetry within an extended Standard Model structure, where the phase transition happens at TeV scales, producing detectable gravitational waves at potential CMB satellite detection ranges. Furthermore, the development of bubble walls in this transition could form microscopic black holes on their surfaces.

A reliable and efficient communication system known as semantic communication aims to minimize data transfer and ensure seamless connectivity to diverse users and services. A fundamental challenge in this process is achieving meaningful and trustworthy interactions between transmitters and receivers through significant information exchange. To address this complexity, this study develops an emergent semantic communication framework based on a sign-based communication system, utilizing causal artificial intelligence to help participants learn and convey important concepts through a cooperative game. A novel neuro-symbolic approach is employed to enable the communication system to perform complex reasoning about cause-and-effect relationships within limited data contexts. By adopting a separation principle, the proposed framework independently optimizes the semantic information content being transmitted, reducing the need for data transmission and thus enhancing overall communication performance.

The Natural Language Processing area has garnered disproportionate interest from researchers in the past. A primary factor driving this interest is the practical use cases enabled by Word Prediction. Improving the user word input experience is the main goal of this process. Namely, the computational load is minimized while the response speed is optimized. To achieve this, a diverse range of methods have been employed, primarily focusing on past and context-based word analysis. In our study, a two-part hybrid algorithm is proposed. The first part utilizes Naive Bayes to quickly identify words aligned with the sentence context, while the second part analyzes the word relationships via a Bayesian model. The output from Part 1 is refined by considering 2D spatial patterns in the text, ultimately yielding words that accurately complete the user's intended sentence meaning. An evaluation of our method demonstrates significant enhancement in prediction accuracy compared to existing techniques.

Recent advancements in Session-based recommendation systems have gained popularity for providing personalized, real-time suggestions with high recall rates compared to conventional techniques. Recent examples include STAMP and NARM models, which, however, did not perform as expected on certain complex sessions containing diverse and non-repetitive user preferences. Our proposed framework addresses this limitation by directly learning the latent features affecting item ranking from training data with actual user interactions, rather than relying on sequential patterns alone. We achieve this by introducing CanR and an optimization process called CanR-Opt that learns CanR from interactions with ranked lists, not just transactional data. Our model offers a flexible design that can incorporate various types of recurrent concepts and demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods on public datasets like Amazon Books and Yahoo! Books.

We examine a pair of particles, similar to DNA bases, suspended in a colloid solution capable of generating activity levels. When subjected to a non-uniform distribution of activity levels, these molecules migrate towards areas with higher activity levels. Our simulated experiments mimic real-world observations and reveal that optimal migration occurs when activity levels have a exponential distribution. Moreover, we develop a mathematical model assuming that each molecule consists of two parts, with randomly attached and detached univalent attachments, where we derive equations describing the probability of activity and compare our predictions with simulated results.

A thorough approach is presented for modeling and simulating discrete fracture-matrix systems, incorporating non-conforming networks, authored by K. S. Keshari, K. S. Keshari, and S. Poulrikas, in the journal's October 2021 issue. The proposed method leverages a novel mesh type, facilitating the use of a mature, dimension-independent simulation technique, Mimetic Finite Difference, while addressing previous limitations of discrete fracture network modeling methods, such as fixed fracture widths and excessive mesh refinement near fracture intersections. By ensuring mass conservation and allowing for disparate fracture and matrix mesh sizes, this method enhances overall efficiency. Numerical examples validate its ability to capture dynamic fracture propagation and transport processes within such systems.

This study introduces an algorithm that utilizes drone swarms to collect and distribute geographic information gathered through flight patterns. As the drones explore, they establish a grid and share their findings with nearby units via communication networks, enabling those not yet exploring to learn of newly discovered locations and integrate into the exploration team. For existing exploration units, this information helps them adjust their routes to cover uncovered terrain areas, effectively maintaining and avoiding conflicts within the formation. This strategy is exemplified using a framework inspired by cellular automata, and its success is demonstrated through computer simulations of diverse scenarios.

This research explores various spectral characteristics of the Seidel matrix associated with a connected chain graph, demonstrating that $-1$ is always an eigenvalue, while other eigenvalues may have a multiplicity of at most two. We derive the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $-1$, the minimum number of unique eigenvalues, and obtain the exact $k$-inertia for $k \ge 3$. In addition, we calculate the Seidel energy of a chain graph, revealing that its minimum value is $n+2$, with the corresponding conditions also specified.

In our investigation, we focus on a mean-field optimal control issue for stochastic differential equations featuring delay, which are influenced by fractional Brownian motion with a Hurst parameter exceeding 0.5. Given the lack of a compensator for this motion, which is typically employed to convert stochastic terms into compensator-based deterministic integrals, we develop a novel driving method to control the finite-variation process arising from the convolution of the fractional Brownian motion. This innovation enables the application of stochastic control techniques to study the value function of the controlled process, which is shown to be smooth under given assumptions. Furthermore, we establish a characterization of this value function and derive sufficient conditions for its optimality.

We've developed a unique, detailed two-parameter set of finite-band Jacobi elliptic potentials that correspond to the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator, seamlessly linking two well-known limit cases, each associated with the absence or presence of elliptic parameters. The associated Dirac spectrum, however, remains unchanged from its Hermitian counterpart, also two-parametered. By examining the transfer matrices for each non-self-adjoint potential, we've obtained precise connections between both sets of spectrum-determining periodic, anti-periodic, and embedded Dirac spectrum small gaps. Furthermore, we've formulated and explored a non-self-adjoint analogue of the Isospectral Hierarchies, with associated non-self-adjoint integrable hierarchies, of which our model is integrable.

As demand for wireless connectivity grows, especially in urban areas, providing reliable and efficient wireless communication is a significant challenge. roadside units (RSUs) meet this demand, yet their range is limited to 300 meters. Extending RSU coverage becomes a necessity. We explore a vehicle relay network architecture and develop a mark renewal process to analyze how long RSUs can stay connected. A two-layer network model consisting of RSUs and vehicle relays is proposed, where the layering pattern greatly influences the network's performance. A mathematical analysis of the connected network is established, and optimization techniques are used to determine the ideal number of vehicle relays per RSU.

Wikipedia's ultimate goal is to be an authoritative reference on various topics.  However, due to a vast number of pages available, a significant portion is considered unlabelled and may require identification as both an opportunity and a challenge for further annotation towards this goal.  The objective of this study is to investigate machine learning techniques that can be employed to label previously unlabelled content by analyzing editing behavior patterns within the repository, thereby assisting in further research and contributing to Wikipedia's mission.  A automatic labeling system is created using templates drawn from already labeled data, providing labeled content as starting point to further machine learning research.

Knowledge distillation is a successful technique for accelerating deep neural networks by training a compact model to mimic the behavior of a high-capacity network. Traditionally, this relies on having access to the original network's training data and parameters, which isn't always feasible due to storage or privacy constraints in real-world applications. This study introduces decision-based black-box knowledge distillation, allowing the training of a faster network to replicate the output of a slower, inaccessible network without requiring access to the original data or parameters, which was previously impossible. The proposed approach achieves a trade-off between model accuracy and size and outperforms existing black-box knowledge distillation techniques when evaluated on the ImageNet dataset.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay mode. The counts of events recorded for these decays were 425.8 and 94.8, respectively. The associated significance level for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay was 3.2 standard deviations. The recorded events for both $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ and $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decays were matched with an unbiased simulation. The calculated branching fraction ratios for the two $B^0_s$ decays into the $D^0$ and $D^0*$ antiparticles and the neutral $K$ particle were calculated and found equal the $10^{-3}$ order of magnitude. The estimated values for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0}K^0_S$ and $B^0_s\to\bar{D^0} K^0_S$ decays were $9.1\times 10^{-6}$ and $22\times

The $C^*$-algebra formalism of topological T-duality developed by Mathai and Rosenberg is applied to a broad class of topological spaces encompassing torus bundles, nilmanifolds, and other examples from string theory. By constructing T-duals from commutative $C^*$-algebras with ${\mathbb R}^n$ action, we establish a simple method for achieving this transformation. Our work rigorously defines these algebraic structures and demonstrates the practical outcomes of this approach within the contexts of string theory and algebraic K-theory.

Reinforcement learning efficiency can be significantly improved through imitation learning by leveraging expert guidance. However, obtaining multiple sets of expert demonstrations for the same task is often impractical or impossible. Our research focuses on a co-imitation approach that bypasses the need for multiple expert demonstrations by training a policy through mutual agreement with other agents on actions that achieve the desired outcome. Our method only demands a single demonstration set, training agents to simulate different contexts. Our simulation tests show that our co-imitation approach produces better results compared to random Imitation Learning (IL) and performs comparably to traditional IL with supervised movement generation (SMG). Our findings also reveal that our method can train effective policies even with diverse and non-optimal expert demonstrations.

This paper proposes a metric function that yields an optimal performance on average, which significantly reduces decoding computations while maintaining superior error-correction capabilities for polarization-adjusted convolutional codes. When using our proposed metric, the PAC code decoder's performance matches that of the convolutional code maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoder in terms of error correction, and even outperforms the polarization-adjusted convolutional codes' list-Viterbi decoder (LIVAC) with a list size of 100, all under binary additive white Gaussian noise channel conditions. Additionally, we suggest a more efficient method to calculate the metric at the decoder, reducing its computational complexity by 66%, by transforming the high-complexity operation into a set of lower-complexity steps. Furthermore, we prove that using our proposed metric with PAC codes results in a distance property that guarantees a minimum distance of $d_{min}=3$, which in turn leads to better error correction and potentially lower error rates.

This project tackles the complex problem of simultaneously monitoring the positions and shapes of hands and objects within a scene, and恢复 their interactions based on a sequence of depth point cloud sequences. Unlike previous research that focused on video sequences, our approach tackles the inherent ambiguity of 3D point clouds by developing a self-supervised hand tracker that tracks hands in the initial frame and propagates these tracks through the video and on to objects. This is achieved by using depth frames to find the best matching keyframes, and using these matches to guide the hand tracker. This is complemented by a hand reconstruction module that uses the tracked hands to improve the quality of the recovered data. Finally, our system predicts the best possible placement of the hands within the point clouds, and uses this information to inform the hand reconstruction and tracking processes. This results in a high quality representation of the hand and object poses, and enables the recovery of hand and object poses that were not present in the original point cloud sequences.

This study employs the modular reduction technique to a Coxeter group of rank 4 featuring a star diagram with 5, 3, and k= 3, 4, 5, or 6 labels, using the odd primes from the ring Z[tau], where tau represents the golden ratio. It categorizes each reduced group as a reflection group over a finite field and demonstrates that the reduced group retains its properties regardless of the used prime in the reduction process.

A novel, markerless extrinsic calibration system is introduced that utilizes a robot-dept camera (RDC) setup, integrating a depth camera and a markerless vision system. Our approach relies on a neural network-based extrinsic calibration and pose estimation method, dubbed the extrinsic calibration and end-effector pose estimator (ECE), to automatically identify the relationship between the robot's depth camera and the world. The proposed system, based on the differentiable volume intersection and volume optimization principles of volume-based extrinsic calibration and end-effector pose estimation (VCEP), leverages learned features from images to efficiently determine the relationship between the RDC setup's depth camera and world frames. As a result, our method offers a more efficient and accurate RDC setup calibration and pose estimation process compared to current approaches. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method's results compare favorably to state-of-the-art volume-based extrinsic calibration and end-effector pose estimation methods as well as a hand-tuned, markerless system.

This study introduces a new framework for analyzing the interplay between various forms of interference in the context of partial interference models. A structured approach is developed to identify instances of multiple interference levels with neighboring units, based on a predefined threshold of effective range. The framework enables researchers to test and detect interunit interference in real-world settings. A simulated and actual randomized experiment setting is examined using this framework to illustrate its practical applications and provide insights into its limitations and and statistical properties.

Calculations of neutrino emissions from self-destructing dark matter particles within a star are being conducted. In the core of a star that has not yet undergone nuclear reactions, it's observed that the interactions between these particles and the star's constituent atoms significantly outlast other processes responsible for neutrino production, including those caused by the star's radioactive isotopes and a phenomenon known as beta decay. Furthermore, in the core of such a star that has undergone nuclear reactions, it's found that the interactions between these particles and the star's constituent atoms significantly outlast the neutrinos produced by lepton pair creation. The outcomes reveal that the energy released by this specific process can remain consistent across a wide range of densities, thereby outlasting the neutrino emissions produced by both pre- and post-exotic nuclear reactions within the star's core. The magnitude of this energy release could be detected through a change in the star's core temperature over time.

The ongoing UNIONS project, the most comprehensive optical survey to date on the Magellanic Clouds, has finished its main survey of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) with a total of 174 million measurements. With additional data expected from the LMC and SMC, the UNIONS/Continued Flux Imaging Survey (CFIS) will provide crucial data for a range of scientific applications, including detailed population analysis and novel studies in gravitational weak lensing. Although the UNIONS data set contains substantial information that can be utilized for wavefront reconstruction, it surpasses traditional studies by several key factors. To process this vast amount of data, we introduce ShapePipe, a new pipeline designed to detect and track objects in images, estimate their shapes, and calculate their redshift. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of our code through a comprehensive shape measurement study and initial GWL analysis on the LMC, revealing the potential for future UNIONS survey uses.

A recent discovery by Pollington and Margulis opened the door for extending the
  equidistribution theory of the Kronecker-Weyl straddle, specifically in relation
  to simultaneous diophantine approximation. This study aims to expand upon
  Pollington and Margulis' work and present new examples related to approximation
  by integers, by integrating integer constraints and analyzing related sequences.
  Findings in this area have implications for understanding the relationship between
  approximations and the legibility of infinite matrices that contain rational entries.

We prove that for k-rational singularities of local complete intersections, k-Du Bois classification applies. For hypersurfaces, k-rationality can be determined based on the minimal exponent. Moreover, certain local vanishing properties for k-rational and k-Du Bois singularities have been identified.

We've observed the appearance of field-induced Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless correlations in a weakly coupled, spin-1/2 Heisenberg material called [Cu(pz)2(2-HOpy)2](PF6)2. Due to a peculiar magnetic arrangement called 'single-ion anisotropy', which arises from the shape of the magnetic energy levels, this material develops a two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet structure when under an in-plane magnetic field. Using advanced measurements and theoretical calculations, we've shown that this 2D structure exhibits a field-dependent temperature correlation pattern that closely mirrors what is predicted by the 2D Heisenberg model. This is the initial demonstration of Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless behavior in a system with an antiferromagnetic order.

Adding three right-handed neutrinos to the Standard Model creates a versatile theoretical framework that can produce dark matter through either a cosmological axion or a heavy sterile neutrino. This model is studied in detail, considering scenarios where one or both dark matter candidates dominate, under assumptions of simplified and more complex model parameters. These analyses serve as a foundation for research articles that explore the implications within specific contexts.

This study optimizes the growth rate of the asymptotic upper limit on the
stabilizer state decomposition required for a single qubit, given by a formula
that grows with the power of $p$ multiplied by the constant, $2^{(1 + \ln d /
\ln p) p}$, where the logarithm is in the natural form. We achieve a substantial
reduction, with a percentage decrease of approximately 17.5, in the exponent of
this formula when using the natural base for logarithms. Furthermore, we
present specific, concrete bounds that demonstrate this improvement, as well
as, that this formula represents a significant enhancement over previously
established bounds, with up to 25% better performance. This formula also
outdoes current research, particularly by providing around 17.5% better than the
bound introduced by Boileau et al. in 2020. Additionally, we present new,
actionable methods that could lead to even greater reductions in the growth rate
of these formulas by at least 7%.

This research employs the Tsallis holographic dark energy model in two scenarios, 
non-interacting and interacting, to calculate essential parameters for the energy 
density equation of state within the FRW universe, also calculating the corresponding pressure.
Furthermore, we investigate two forms of the quintessence model - a complex and a real form.
We then compare these two forms by examining their respective equations of state and pressure, 
as well as discussing any implications this comparison may have.
In addition, we resolve an interesting issue arising from our calculations by demonstrating 
how a complex form of the quintessence model can contribute to resolving a conflict between theory and observation in cosmology.

Between October 2019 and January 2020, the LAMOST performed a unique observational experiment using four sets of 4888 spectra, each collected from $K2$ observations, resulting in 1,542,453 unique spectra of 1,368,149 individual stars. The majority of these stars were found to be located near the galactic plane and conform to the main sequence of the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram. In contrast, the spectral distributions along the galactic latitude showed little variation. The LAMOST's data revealed significantly more transient events than anticipated, significantly exceeding 10 times the expected occurrences. The spectral events categorised into three main groups: those caused by active galactic nucleus disk flickering, binary systems with eclipsing variable stars, and transiting exoplanets. The LAMOST's vast dataset offers a highly comprehensive view of the sky, surpassing existing surveys such as Pan-STARRS1 and eROSITA by over 100 times, thereby providing an extensive foundation for the LAMOST TDS to further its research.

Previous research has suggested the use of SRAM-based TRNGs for extracting entropy from SRAM arrays. As these arrays are commonly employed in caching scenarios and exhibit irregularities due to manufacturing discrepancies, SRAM-based TRNGs have become a viable option. Nonetheless, the employment of such TRNGs poses an entry-exit dilemma since an SRAM array serving as a source of randomness must also function reliably for data storage, entry, and exit. Resolving this problem, a new method, termed TuRaN, utilizes SRAM voltage undersupply to leverage SRAM entropy without encountering the aforementioned dilemma. By implementing SRAM voltage undersupply to induce logical bit-flips, SRAM-based TRNGs can be integrated seamlessly into system architectures, solely for enhancing randomness quality, without impacting the storage reliability. The underlying bit-flip mechanism resulting from voltage undersupply allows for supply voltage-induced TRNGs with proven reliability. The effectiveness of TuRaN is evaluated by comparing its design to other SRAM-based TRNG designs using entropy metrics, information theoretic security analysis, and practical test suites. The experimental results indicate that the employment of SRAM voltage undersupply produces high-quality random patterns meeting industry standards, and are capable of withstanding the effects of process variations, duty-cycle fluctuations, and temperature changes.

A preliminary design and simulation of a single-electron resistive switch has been developed, incorporating two linear molecules that interact electrostatically: one molecule is a tunnel barrier with electrically isolated single electrons and the other is a tunnel barrier made of a quantum emitter with a fixed dipole moment. Notably, this switch's resistance exhibits a periodic variation in relation to the electric field of the quantum emitter and shows distinct hysteresis behavior based on its initial configuration.

The concept of loop-tree duality has emerged as a promising approach for numerically computing complex multi-loop scattering amplitudes, offering a significant shift from traditional methods. In this framework, universal numerical cancellation is achieved across all loop iterations, in contrast to lower-order methods that require precise angle evaluations. While initial applications were limited to one-loop diagrams with simple propagators, recent advancements have extended loop-tree duality to diagrams involving general powers of propagators and virtual particles. This extension enables the cancellation of singularities associated with branch points, a crucial step in automating multi-loop numerical calculations. In this study, we explore the extension of loop-tree duality to a class of diagrams containing vacuum diagrams with multiple loop branches. These diagrams are chosen for their simplicity and relevance, as they can be automatically identified through a numerical evaluation strategy that remains valid for any diagram iteration. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of loop-tree duality in this specific class of diagrams, and suggest its potential for automating multi-loop calculations in quantum field theory.

This paper aims to provide a direct eigenfunction expansion formula for the one-dimensional two-state quantum walk's transition function. It also seeks to establish a pointwise asymptotic formula for the given transition function as it extends infinitely. In order to achieve this goal, the paper uses a previously derived eigenfunction expansion formula by Kitagawa and Yoshida and analyses the spectral measure's asymptotic behavior. Additionally, the paper considers an alternative approach by adapting the methods from the author's earlier study on the discrete Schrödinger equation. In particular, the paper derives a new dispersion relation for the one-two state quantum walk, resulting in a new eigenfunction expansion formula for its transition function. Ultimately, the paper obtains the desired pointwise asymptotic formula for the given transition function.

This study examines the composition of hybrid stars formed by neutrons, protons, and various other particles. The analysis combines the Sigma-omega-rho model for a specific nuclear phase with two distinct quark phase models, and incorporates Maxwell and Gibbs conditions to understand the phase transition. By analyzing mass-radius relations, a hybrid star's mass is predicted to be limited to twice the mass of the sun.

The introduction of $q$-deformation into optomechanical systems reveals opportunities to amplify non-traditional optical phenomena. This investigation explores the optical behavior of a linearly coupled $q$-deformed optomechanical system, comprised of two optical cavities interacting with a shared mechanical element, within the context of the Harosie deformation model. By incorporating the $q$-deformation operator into the Harosie state, we demonstrate that optical behavior can be amplified beyond initial expectations. Furthermore, both theoretical calculations and numerical analyses reveal the potential to enhance light speed, accompanied by simultaneous reduction in noise.

In a previous study, I developed a model where the Two-Rotors Model's negative scissors states, consisting of two-dimensional dynamical symmetry breaking, were shown to consist of two distinct one-dimensional irreducible representations. These primary and secondary rotors contribute equally to the negative and positive R-parity sectors. According to the model, states with negative R-parity and positive R- and J-values can only exist when the angular momentum of one rotor is non-zero. Furthermore, I established that the relative strengths of the E1 transitions between these and the R-odd states with positive J-values are in agreement with experimental data.
